scope: Native Windows GUI regression with an isolated profile and a synthetic local Sender; WAV files and private screenshots are not published.
build_status: Intermediate runtime-tested build before the last footer removal and subsequent plug-in full-save worker changes; not the final packaged binary hash.
ui_observations: All seven History choices were visible in the native dropdown.
10s -> 600s -> 60s -> 10s changes remained operable with no long stall observed; this is not a timed latency measurement.
After Pause, a native endpoint drag formed an approximately 19.77-second selection.
Play resumed capture while the displayed picture/flags stayed fixed and the red LED/dBFS kept updating.
After live History was reduced to 10 seconds and more than 10 seconds elapsed, the selection still displayed approximately 19.77 seconds.
Alt+grave saved the selected material and returned the view to live.
Native zoom changed the visible range and guide density.
limitations: The baseline snapshot is 39.98 seconds because its longer history was still filling; it is not a verified 60-second export.
The later selection file is 19.768083333333333 seconds, consistent with the UI-rounded 19.77-second range, but no expected source start/end sample sequence was compared.
Finite stored samples and duration do not prove absence of dropped/duplicated frames or audible artifacts.
The run used one stereo synthetic Sender, not a native dual-source A/B verification.
No physical native Shift-drag was tested; modifier behavior is covered separately by RawInput/shared tests.
Native window resizing and the final rebuilt UI-copy cleanup were not completed in this observed run.
No end-to-end latency, DAW/macOS performance, or new GPU/CPU monitoring is inferred.
